name: YOWIE Hotel & Shop
sourceName: YOWIE Guide: Black-Owned Businesses in the South Street Area
ownershipEvidence: The source guide identifies YOWIE among Black-owned businesses on South Street and describes co-founder Shannon Maldonado.
notes: Physical South Street business; address and customer-facing shop URL are published in the source guide. The source also describes a boutique hotel, but this record is for the shop.

name: Moore Vintage Archive
sourceName: YOWIE Guide: Black-Owned Businesses in the South Street Area
ownershipEvidence: The source guide includes Moore Vintage Archive in its Black-owned South Street-area business guide and names owner Keesean.
notes: Physical Queen Village/Fabric Row business; source guide provides address and describes designer vintage womenswear. Official customer destination and address were corroborated on the business contact page.

name: South Street Art Mart
sourceName: YOWIE Guide: Black-Owned Businesses in the South Street Area
ownershipEvidence: The source guide explicitly describes South Street Art Mart as queer-owned and artist-run; the business website describes it as queer woman owned.
notes: Physical South Street-area retail shop. Included because the starting guide covers diverse community-owned businesses; no Black/Latino ownership is inferred.

name: Black and Nobel
sourceName: YOWIE Guide: Black-Owned Businesses in the South Street Area
ownershipEvidence: The source guide explicitly describes Black and Nobel as a Black-owned bookstore and cultural hub.
notes: Physical South Street business; phone and address are supported by the business social/search listing, while the guide supplies the ownership and business description.

name: Atomic City Comics
sourceName: YOWIE Guide: Black-Owned Businesses in the South Street Area
ownershipEvidence: The source guide explicitly describes Atomic City Comics as a long-standing Black-owned comic book shop and names owner Darryl Jones.
notes: Physical South Street business; customer-facing website, social pages, phone, and address are published or corroborated by the business destinations.

name: Marsha's
sourceName: YOWIE Guide: Black-Owned Businesses in the South Street Area
ownershipEvidence: The source guide describes Marsha's as Philadelphia's first all-women's sports bar but does not state racial or diaspora ownership.
notes: Physical South Street business included as a community-relevant consumer business; ownership is not inferred beyond the published all-women-focused description.

name: Loomen Labs
sourceName: YOWIE Guide: Black-Owned Businesses in the South Street Area
ownershipEvidence: The source guide names founder Jordan Lee Cook but does not state Black, Latino, or diaspora ownership.
notes: Physical South Street business included from the starting guide; ownership identity is not inferred. Official website confirms 322 South Street and customer offerings.

name: Casa México
sourceName: Visit Philadelphia: A Guide to South Philly Barbacoa & Casa México
ownershipEvidence: Visit Philadelphia's Latino Philadelphia coverage identifies Casa México as part of the city's Latin cuisine scene and names chef Cristina Martinez; the linked guide supplies the South Philadelphia address and phone.
notes: Physical South 9th Street business. Latino designation is based on Visit Philadelphia's Latino-focused coverage and published chef/business context; no further identity detail is inferred.

name: South Philly Barbacoa
sourceName: Visit Philadelphia: A Guide to South Philly Barbacoa & Casa México
ownershipEvidence: Visit Philadelphia's Latino Philadelphia coverage identifies chef Cristina Martinez and South Philly Barbacoa as part of Philly's Latin cuisine; the business menu page identifies the 1140 S 9th Street location.
notes: Physical South 9th Street business. The address differs from Casa México and is supported by the official chef website menu PDF; hours are not carried into this record.

name: Association of Mexican Business Owners of Philadelphia (AEM / AMBOP)
ownershipEvidence: The Sabores campaign identifies AEM / AMBOP as the Association of Mexican Business Owners of Philadelphia and campaign creator.
notes: Community resource rather than a commercial map pin. The campaign states it amplifies Latino-owned businesses along the 9th Street corridor and surrounding streets, but its dynamically rendered directory returned zero businesses in text extraction, so no additional participant records were fabricated.
